stem: A food manufacturing study measures the weight (grams) for a sample of 30 cereal boxes. The sample mean is 299.6 g with a sample standard deviation of 30.0 g. However, 2 of the 30 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 28 observations have a mean of 292.2 g and standard deviation of 20.6 g. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 299.6, 95% CI = [288.4, 310.8]. Without outliers: mean = 292.2, 95% CI = [284.4, 300.0]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [284.4, 310.8]. Point estimate: 295.9 g.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [284.4, 310.8].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
